t: G17 Experimentation Engine: Monte Carlo Estimator — Simple
name: G17 Experimentation Engine: Monte Carlo Estimator — Simple
title: G17 Experimentation Engine: Monte Carlo Estimator — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The honest workhorse of simulation: estimate an expectation by averaging samples, with the error shrinking as 1/√N. The sample budget is computed from the target error before a single sample is drawn — no experiment runs open-ended. The demo estimates π by dart-throwing and checks the error against the bound.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Samples for 1% Monte Carlo error = 10000 samples. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Monte Carlo with 1/√N convergence is the real, standard method across physics and finance.
signature_version: Signature version: the RSC estimator — the chapter's Reality Simulation Constant as the estimator's calibration target, with the 'simulates reality' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: set the error target, compute N, draw the samples, and report estimate ± bound.
math_note: Samples for 1% Monte Carlo error: 10000 samples [verified]; Samples for 0.1% error: 1000000 samples [verified]
safety: No hazard; never report an estimate without its error bound.
how_it_works: Draw N samples, average, and report the estimate ± 1/√N. The budget step inverts the bound: N = (1/error)². The demo runs the estimator and verifies the empirical error respects the computed bound.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub

name: G17 Experimentation Engine: Experiment Ledger — Intermediate
title: G17 Experimentation Engine: Experiment Ledger — Intermediate
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The lab notebook as a machine: every experiment registered before it runs, every result recorded with its seed and bound, every negative result kept. The ledger is what separates an engine from a story — preregistration plus complete records.

One level deeper. Headline number: Ledger entries for a 20-run campaign = 20 entries. The how-it-works section adds the working mechanism; the math checks below show each claim beside its recomputed value.

real_world_basis: Preregistration and complete reporting are real scientific standards this ledger mechanizes.
signature_version: Signature version: the RSC ledger — the chapter's constant as the ledger's completeness target, with the 'all experiments' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: create the registry, require registration before runs, and audit for missing results.
math_note: Ledger entries for a 20-run campaign: 20 entries [verified]; Hash-collision odds across 1M ledger entries (128-bit): 1.469e-27 probability [verified]

math_check.label: Ledger entries for a 20-run campaign
math_check.note: corrected 2026-10-19: formula was 2^n, unrelated to the claim

safety: No hazard; the failure mode is a ledger with gaps — audit it.
how_it_works: Register the design, run under the harness, and file the result with seed, N, bound, and outcome. Negative results file identically to positive ones. The demo writes a ledger entry.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
